rule.description: A function (counting the closures it defines) that reads or writes at least three distinct fields of repository-declared classes, with that foreign interest exceeding its own this-field accesses, has its record-keeping interest in another owner's data instead of coordinating through the owner's behavior.

checks.description: Detect module-level functions, including the closures they define, whose distinct (class, field) pairs over repository-declared class instances reach at least three and exceed the function's own this-field accesses.
checks.detected_relation: cache-boundary function -> fields of the cache record and cache registry classes
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The function's primary interest is state another structure owns: it decides record matching, settlement outcome, expiry and eviction by reading and writing record fields from the outside instead of asking the owning structure to do so. That misplaced interest is the envy relation; relocating the decisions onto the data-owning classes dissolves it without any renaming trick.

matches.evidence: The render-phase coordinator iterates the registry's entries array, re-implements key matching against entry.keys with entry.equal, probes 'error'/'response' presence on the record, cancels and rewrites entry.timeout, reads entry.remove and entry.promise, assigns the removal closure and the promise-settlement chain onto the fresh record, assigns entry.response and entry.error from its callbacks, and throws entry.promise: 8 distinct foreign fields (CacheRegistry{entries}; CacheEntry{keys,equal,error,timeout,remove,response,promise}), 0 own accesses.

The inspection helper scans the registry's entries array itself, re-implements key matching against entry.keys with entry.equal, and reads the settled value through optional chaining on the record: 4 distinct foreign fields (CacheRegistry{entries}; CacheEntry{response,keys,equal}), 0 own accesses.

The invalidation helper drains the registry's entries array by splice, and for a keyed removal scans it, re-implements key matching against entry.keys with entry.equal, then splices the record out by index: 3 distinct foreign fields (CacheRegistry{entries}; CacheEntry{keys,equal}), 0 own accesses.

excluded.reason: Accesses inside a class through this are own-data accesses; foreign method calls (coordination) are not counted as data use.
They operate on plain arrays and thenables; their parameters carry no repository-declared class-instance data, so no cross-class interest exists there.
Single-expression forwarders to the coordinator: no independent record-field decisions of their own, so they are passive callers rather than locations of the smell.
Test and build support exercise the public API only and are outside the analyzed cache-boundary surface.
